summary: Sudden 5xx wave from ephemeral port exhaustion and runtime restart cascade affecting dedicated tenant
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-12 09:42 UTC we observed a rapid increase in 5xx responses for a NeuroDeck tenant in us-east-1. Errors manifested as 502/503 from the API gateway and a series of upstream serving-runtime restarts for the tenant's dedicated pool. Impact: Customer-facing traffic for NeuroDeck (dedicated) saw ~40% error rate for 20 minutes across text-generation endpoints. Production impact was degraded UX for active users and elevated alerting across SRE/SUPPORT.
timeline:
2026-03-12 09:38 UTC - First alert: api-gateway 5xx rate from tenant T-9423.
2026-03-12 09:42 UTC - Support ticket opened; automated mitigation attempted (traffic reroute).
2026-03-12 09:45 UTC - SRE observed repeated runtime container restarts and api-gateway accept failures.
2026-03-12 10:00 UTC - Temporary mitigation: scale-down tenant prefetch concurrency and restart runtime pool.
2026-03-12 10:12 UTC - Error rate drops to baseline.
2026-03-13 02:10 UTC - Regressed briefly during low traffic with similar symptoms; created follow-up investigation.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Issue is load/tenant specific; reproducible by issuing a sustained burst of short-running streaming generation requests to the customer's pinned model from multiple ephemeral clients (high-conn churn).
2) Observe api-gateway 502/503 with upstream connect errors and runtime container OOM/restart sequence within 5-10 minutes.
3) Resource and socket metrics show growing number of TIME_WAIT sockets and per-process fd usage climbing toward limit.
logs:
API gateway logs (sample):
[2026-03-12T09:41:12Z] tenant=T-9423 route=/v1/generate status=502 upstream_error=connect_reset
[2026-03-12T09:41:13Z] tenant=T-9423 route=/v1/generate status=503 upstream_error=accept_failed: EMFILE
Serving-runtime stderr (container):
2026-03-12T09:41:14Z runtime: panic: runtime out of memory
... goroutine 182 [running]:
runtime.throw(0xabc123)
...
kernel socket stats (excerpt):
netstat -an | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l => 18934
ss -s indicates high orphan sockets and many sockets in TIME_WAIT from ephemeral ports
investigation_notes:
Initial findings:
- api-gateway started returning EMFILE/accept_failed indicating per-process fd exhaustion on the proxy worker.
- Concurrently, serving-runtime pods for the tenant entered repeated OOM/restart cycles; container logs indicate small but persistent GPU memory fragmentation leak under high-connection-churn workloads.
- Network metrics show high ephemeral port churn (TIME_WAIT counts ~19k) originating from a burst of short-lived streaming sessions from the customer's integration test harness.
Hypothesis: A combination of (1) a tenant-initiated high-churn burst of short TCP connections (streaming clients without connection reuse) and (2) a latent memory fragmentation bug in the dedicated serving-runtime caused resource exhaustion at both OS fd level (api-gateway) and GPU memory (runtime). The fd exhaustion caused accept failures at the gateway, amplifying retries and increasing pressure on the runtime, leading to a restart cascade and elevated 5xx rate.
Corroborating evidence: fd counters on the api-gateway node peaked just before runtime restarts; restarting the gateway workers freed fds and immediately reduced 5xxs while runtime restarts persisted until runtime pool was recycled.
mitigation_actions:
Short-term (complete):
- Scoped traffic reroute for T-9423 away from hot gateway nodes (09:44 UTC).
- Reduced tenant prefetch/concurrency caps for NeuroDeck to 2 concurrent streams per-client (09:50 UTC).
- Restarted serving-runtime pool for the tenant to clear GPU memory fragmentation (10:00 UTC).
- Increased per-worker file descriptor soft-limit on api-gateway nodes from 4096 -> 16384 (applied 10:05 UTC) as emergency measure.
Long-term (in progress):
- Patch runtime memory fragmentation (PR opened).
- Add autoscaling backpressure for high-conn-churn patterns.
- Harden api-gateway to recycle workers earlier when fd pressure detected and implement passive connection re-use heuristics.
next_steps:
1) Engineering to complete runtime memory-fix PR and schedule a canary in staging (owner: eng/runtime team, PR #4823).
2) Networking to review kernel parameters for ephemeral port range and TCP reuse to reduce TIME_WAIT amplification (owner: infra/network).
3) Product ops to add tenant-level protection rule to limit short-lived streaming connection churn per-second (owner: platform).
4) Schedule postmortem and runbook update (owner: SRE).

2026-03-12T10:20Z - Support (to Customer - NeuroDeck): We applied temporary concurrency limits and restarted the runtime pool. That reduced the error rate. We will follow up with a timeline to prevent recurrence.

resolution: Mitigation applied: concurrency caps, gateway worker rotation, runtime pool restart. Root cause under engineering investigation (memory fragmentation + ephemeral socket exhaustion). Patch PR created; scheduled staging canary. No permanent code fix deployed yet.
postmortem_plan: Postmortem scheduled: 2026-03-18 15:00 UTC. Topics: reproduce load profile, confirm fix in staging, update runbooks for fd pressure, implement tenant-level backpressure policies.
